summary: I recomputed every quoted R2, control, margin, normalised margin, layer pick, val_mse_ratio and trajectory figure for the four findings against raw_evidence. Most values check out. f-838c's earlier review issue was answered and the downgrade to inconclusive was applied. The main problem is in f-8dea: it says probes_final has no layer-1 force R2, but it does (0.8211). f-dd1c has small trajectory misquotes and leaves out the N=64 run it relies on. The last 5 experiments stay on the width-scaling questions, and the new seed-24 d64 arms pre-register a fixed layer 1 in response to the earlier review, so there is no drift.

issues.message: The claim says 'probes_final does not give layer-1 force R2'. It does: force layer 1 = 0.8211 (control 0.598, spread 0.0175, margin 0.2231). That is +0.011 over the d128 layer-1 reference of 0.81015, so on the confidence note's own stated test ('a layer-1 value within 0.03 of 0.81015 would support it') the data already exists. The best-margin pick is noise: layer 3 margin 0.2295 vs layer 1 margin 0.2231, a difference of 0.0064, below the control spreads of 0.0171 and 0.0175. So the formal expected_if_false hit (layer 3, 0.8435 > 0.84) and the layer-1 saturation reading rest on a noise-level layer choice. Correct the record and state the layer-1 result explicitly. Minor: 'layer 3 elsewhere' is wrong for steps 0-1000, where the best layer is layer 1.

Gap trajectory: step 500 is 0.7287 - 0.6930 = 0.036, not within the quoted 0.042-0.044 band for steps 500-1500 (steps 1000 and 1500 give 0.042 and 0.044). The note says N=128 force is 'still rising about +0.003-0.004 per 500 steps', but the last three intervals are +0.0016, +0.0037 and +0.0011, a mean of about 0.002. N=64 normalised accel_step is quoted as about 0.867; the raw value is 0.1818/0.2093 = 0.869. None of these change the verdict.

The pre-registration requires both arms' run IDs to be cited as evidence and all values to come from unrounded probes_final. evidence_run_ids lists only run-20261016-072048-0756, and the N=64 values are taken from 'trajectory, about 0.834'. The paired run-20261016-070351-7571 is complete. Its probes_final layer-1 force is 0.8339 (control 0.6096), which gives an exact same-layer gap of 0.0710. Add that run and use its probes_final values.

The matched-loss check the note calls impossible can be done from the data here. N=64 val_mse_ratio reaches 0.01325 at step 3500, close to N=128's 0.01258 at step 6000. N=64 layer-1 force at step 3500 is 0.8168, a gap of 0.054, which is still at least 0.04. Caveat: baseline_cv_mse differs about 16x between N=64 and N=128, so ratio matching across N is approximate.

responses.response: Accepted. probes_final does report layer-1 force for run-20261016-073808-5555: R2 0.8211 (control 0.598, spread 0.0175, margin 0.2231). Against the d128 layer-1 reference of 0.81015 that is a same-layer change of +0.011, inside the 0.03 saturation band, so by the test stated in the confidence note, layer-1 N=64 force is width-saturated for seed 23. The best-margin pick of layer 3 (margin 0.2295 vs layer 1's 0.2231, a difference of 0.0064) is smaller than either layer's control spread (0.0171 and 0.0175), so it is noise. The formal expected_if_false hit (layer-3 R2 0.8435 > 0.84) rests on that noise-level choice and is also cross-layer against d128 layer 1. Seed 23 therefore shows the same split as seed 22: flat at layer 1 and higher at a later layer. Under the hypothesis as pre-registered (best-margin layer), neither branch holds cleanly, so the status stays inconclusive. One correction to the trajectory description: the best layer is layer 1 at steps 0-1000 as well as at 2500 and 3500, so 'layer 3 elsewhere' is wrong for the early checkpoints. Pending and queued width arms already score at fixed layer 1 with layer 4 as secondary, and I have filed a new question on whether the width gain is confined to layers after layer 1.

Accepted. The same-layer gap is 0.036 at step 500 (0.7287 - 0.6930), then 0.042 at step 1000 and 0.044 at step 1500. The early band should read 0.036-0.044, and the gap widens to about 0.07 by step 4000. N=128 force growth over the last three 500-step intervals is +0.0016, +0.0037 and +0.0011, a mean of about 0.002 per 500 steps, not 0.003-0.004. N=64 normalised accel_step is 0.1818/0.2093 = 0.869. None of these change the verdict.

Accepted. run-20261016-070351-7571 should be cited alongside run-20261016-072048-0756, and its probes_final values used. Layer 1 is the best-margin force layer in both arms. N=64 0.8339 (control 0.6096) minus N=128 0.76291 (control 0.60417) gives an exact same-layer gap of 0.0710 with a control difference of 0.0054, so the deficit is in trained R2. The accel_step comparison at layer 4, also from probes_final, gives normalised margins of 0.869 (N=64) and 0.864 (N=128). Every criterion still holds with the exact values, so the status stays supported (single seed). This repeats the citation omission accepted earlier on f-20261016-022923-3654 and f-20261016-032946-f8ef. This cycle's proposal lists every reference run ID in the hypothesis text so the analysis step cites them.
